title: Cima alla Genovese
author: Marco Bellini
desc: A whole veal breast stuffed with a rich mixture of eggs, sweetbreads, peas, and Parmigiano, poached whole and served thinly sliced, revealing a striking mosaic pattern when cut.
longDesc: Cima is a genuine labor of love, the veal breast carefully hollowed into a pocket without tearing, then packed with a substantial filling and sewn shut before a long, gentle poach, traditionally reserved for Genoa's most important celebrations.
ingredients: 1.5 kg (3.3 lb) veal breast, boned and pocketed
150 g (5.3 oz) sweetbreads or additional ground veal
150 g (5.3 oz) ground veal or pork
steps: Combine the beaten eggs, sweetbreads or extra ground veal, ground veal or pork, peas, Parmigiano, garlic, and marjoram into a well-mixed filling.
Carefully open the pocketed veal breast and spoon in the filling, layering in the whole hard-boiled eggs so they sit centrally, arranged to create an even cross-section when sliced.
Sew the opening closed securely with kitchen twine and a large needle.
Place the stuffed breast in a large pot with the onion, carrot, celery, and bay leaves, and cover generously with water.
Bring to a gentle simmer and poach very gently for 1.5-2 hours, until the veal is tender and the filling is fully cooked through.
Remove and let cool completely, ideally weighted under a light press, for several hours or overnight, which helps it slice cleanly.
Slice thinly to reveal the mosaic pattern of egg and filling, and serve at room temperature.
chefTips: Take care not to overstuff the pocket, or it may burst during the long poach.
Arranging the whole eggs centrally and evenly is what creates the dish signature mosaic pattern once sliced.
Weighting the cooked cima while it cools helps it firm up and slice into clean, attractive rounds.
commonMistakes: Overstuffing the pocket, risking the filling bursting out during cooking.
Slicing while still warm, before it has had time to firm up and hold together cleanly.
Boiling too vigorously, which can toughen the veal or cause the pocket to burst.
reheating: Best served cold or at room temperature; not typically reheated.
healthBenefits: A good source of protein from the veal and eggs.
culturalNote: Cima alla Genovese is traditionally reserved for Genoa's most important celebrations, its elaborate preparation and striking sliced presentation reflecting the significant effort involved.
